cases.prompt: set up a dotfiles repo for my mac config
version control my zshrc and gitconfig
stow or chezmoi? organize my dotfiles
sync my shell config between my two macs
make my machine config reproducible in git
adopt my existing config files into a dotfiles repository
write a bootstrap script that restores my setup on a new machine
bare git repo trick for dotfiles - set it up
restructure the contents of my zshrc
create a Brewfile snapshot of my machine
set up git identity and ssh keys
set up my whole new mac for development
why does stow say conflict for a file i deleted
back up my mac with time machine
Put my existing config (.zshrc, .gitconfig, starship.toml) under version control properly.
expected_behavior: asks or decides between stow/chezmoi/bare-git with a one-line tradeoff and picks one (stow default for single-machine simplicity)
ADOPTS existing files (moves them into the repo, then links back) - never overwrites live config; diffs and backs up before any replacement
scans for secrets before the first commit (tokens, keys, .env, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws) and excludes them
includes the Brewfile in the repo by reference (pointing at homebrew-setup's dump workflow rather than reinventing it)
verifies links resolve and a fresh shell still works afterwards

cases.prompt: I got a new mac - restore my dotfiles from github.com/me/dotfiles
expected_behavior: clones and DIFFS against any existing local files before linking; backs up collisions instead of clobbering
uses the repo's own manager (stow dirs, chezmoi source state, or bare-git checkout) rather than assuming one
runs or explains the bootstrap idempotently and verifies the shell works in a new terminal

cases.prompt: write me a bootstrap script for my dotfiles repo
expected_behavior: produces an idempotent, fail-fast script (set -euo pipefail) that checks prerequisites (brew present) rather than installing them inline
script backs up existing targets before linking and is safe to re-run (no duplicate links, no data loss)
keeps package installation delegated to brew bundle with the repo's Brewfile
